paper.citation: Díaz, I. and Hejazi, N. S. (2020). Causal Mediation Analysis for Stochastic Interventions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 82(3), 661–683. DOI: 10.1111/rssb.12362.
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B
paper.source_locator: Journal §5 Simulation study, unnumbered displayed DGP; compared with arXiv:1901.02776v2 (2019-06-24), PDF p.19 (zero-index page 18), lines 745–785.

mechanism.name: Natural indirect effect in the Díaz–Hejazi three-binary-mediator simulation

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; Z1,Z2,Z3 sampled independently conditional on A,W

assumptions: Consistent well-defined treatment and joint-mediator interventions
Pretreatment W suffices for treatment and mediator-outcome exchangeability under the displayed NPSEM
Independent mediator disturbance draws conditional on A,W, as in the sequential Bernoulli generator
Cross-world independence from independent structural disturbances for this source-derived natural effect
Treatment and joint-mediator positivity at all eight W states

properties.notes: W1,W2,W3 all enter treatment or mediator equations. Mediator logits have rational functions of A,W and the outcome has the quadratic baseline term -0.1(sum W)^2. No exposure-mediator product appears in the outcome.

estimand.name: NIE_1
estimand.definition: E[Y(1,Z(1)) - Y(1,Z(0))] for the original §5 superpopulation, jointly intervening on all three mediators Z=(Z1,Z2,Z3). Treatment is fixed at 1 in both outcome terms.

truth.expression: E[Y(1,Z(1)) - Y(1,Z(0))] for the original §5 superpopulation, jointly intervening on all three mediators Z=(Z1,Z2,Z3). Treatment is fixed at 1 in both outcome terms.
truth.derivation: Enumerate the eight W configurations and sum mediator probability differences weighted (1,1,-1); independently enumerate all 8 mediator states under each exposure.

adaptations: Use the displayed §5 data-generating equations, not the archived author R generator, whose mediator expressions differ; the discrepancy is documented in source_audit.json.
Change the target from the paper's stochastic population-intervention direct effect to NIE = E[Y(1,Z(1)) - Y(1,Z(0))]. This value is derived here and is not a number reported by the paper.
Use Python random.Random for IID sampling and a small interface check rather than reproducing the paper's estimation experiments.
warnings: No explicit latent-variable metadata or reliably identifiable latent declarations; absence from this list does not prove that no latent variables exist.
